question: What is the MINIMUM duration of symptoms required to diagnose a full manic episode (as opposed to hypomania)?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Two days is insufficient for either mania or hypomania by diagnostic criteria.
Four days is the minimum duration for a HYPOMANIC episode, not a full manic episode.

answers.text: At least 1 week (or any duration if hospitalisation required)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A full manic episode requires ≥1 week of abnormally elevated/expansive/irritable mood and increased energy, or any duration if the episode is severe enough to warrant hospitalisation or there is psychosis.
Two weeks is the minimum for a Major Depressive Episode, not mania. Mania has a lower duration threshold (≥1 week) and is defined partly by severity and functional impact.

overallFeedback.feedback: A common mix-up: mania requires ≥1 week (or hospitalisation/psychosis), hypomania requires ≥4 days. A full MDE requires ≥2 weeks. These three thresholds are worth memorising as a set.
Well recalled. The mania ≥1 week / hypomania ≥4 days distinction is a high-yield differentiator for bipolar I vs bipolar II.
